annotations.text:
THE DELIVERABLE
What `franking -html report.html ./reports` writes.

One self-contained file: inlined CSS and JS, no CDN, no web fonts, no network. Filter chips, sortable columns and search all work — click them.

Order is inverted from stdout: verdict, then actions, then the full table. The payload comes first.

ONE RULE THE TEMPLATE MUST KEEP
A DMARC pass is the UNION of aligned DKIM and aligned SPF, so it cannot be derived from the two percentages — 62% + 41% is not 100%, and capping the sum silently promotes a half-broken sender to passing.

The Go side already counts it per record. The template must carry that count through, never recompute it from the columns.

THE COMMON CASE
Most runs are clean, so the all-clear state has to read as calm and finished rather than empty.

The actions section becomes a statement, not a blank panel, and the policy note turns into the one piece of advice that matters: you can tighten now.

Controls are dropped here on purpose — under three rows there is nothing to filter.

PHONE
The seven-column table collapses to one stacked record per address.

The phone drops COLUMNS, never findings: every action group and every filter chip that the desktop renders is here too.

Chips are 44px.

PRINT / PDF
A4 at 96px/inch. The tint, the controls and the reverse-name column all drop; the pass bar becomes hairline-bounded so it does not drink ink.

Reading copy — prose, advice, action rows — sits at the 12pt floor (16px). Subordinate labels and the footer go to 10.5pt, no lower.

THE VOCABULARY
What the Go template implements: five class marks, three file statuses, the type scale and the font stacks.

Hue and lightness both vary across the five, so colour alone is never the signal — the name and the rule carry it. Rightmost column on each row is the same mark in grayscale, as the proof.
